text:
jess: Hey team — customer bob@acme reported weird embed dimension flips: sometimes their index ingestion fails with dimension mismatch. They say embeddings endpoint returns 512 for some requests and 768 for others.

matt: Do we have any multi-model routing for that tenant? Could be model variant fallback.

customer-ops-bob: Repro steps I got from them: they call /v1/embeddings with model=embed-v1-small, but our proxy rewrites model param to embed-v1-small:fast occasionally. They said this started after a rollout yesterday.

sophia: Hmm that could explain a mismatch if the cache key doesn't include the exact model tag. But why would the dims change between 512 and 768 — those are two different model families.

jess: I looked at logs for tenant acme-123. Here's an excerpt: 

```
INFO 2025-06-04T15:12:03Z req=abc123 tenant=acme-123 model=embed-v1-small dim=512 cache_key=tenant:acme-123:embed-v1-small prefix=user:12345 hit=false
INFO 2025-06-04T15:12:03Z req=abc124 tenant=acme-123 model=embed-v1-large dim=768 cache_key=acme-123:embed-v1-small prefix=user:12345 hit=true
ERROR 2025-06-04T15:12:03Z ingestion=ingest-xyz dimension_mismatch expected=768 got=512
```

matt: Wait that second line shows model=embed-v1-large but cache_key has embed-v1-small. That indicates cache key generation is dropping the model id or being normalized incorrectly.

sophia: Also note the cache_key prefixes — sometimes we use `tenant:acme-123:` and other times `acme-123:`. That smells like prefix reuse across SDK codepaths. If the prefix normalization is inconsistent, two different requests can collide.

customer-ops-bob: I asked the customer to capture two full request/response pairs. They sent them: 

Request A (produced 512 vector):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
{ "model": "embed-v1-small", "input": "Hello" }
```
Response A: dim=512, vector[0..3]=[0.12, -0.04, ...]

Request B (produced 768 vector):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
{ "model": "embed-v1-large", "input": "Hello" }
```
Response B: dim=768, vector[0..3]=[0.21, -0.07, ...]

customer-ops-bob: They swear they always call embed-v1-small. But the proxy logs show occasional rewriting. They suspect a canary of embed-v1-large was routed to the same pool.

jess: Repro attempt on our side: I sent 1000 rapid requests with mixed model names and observed cache hits where model name in cache_key didn't match request model. Minimal repro script: 

```
for i in seq 1 1000; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-v1-small","input":"test"}' &
done
```

Then grep logs for cache_key != model. Got ~0.8% mismatches.

matt: That % correlates with the number of requests hitting a specific prefix-normalization path in the SDK. There's a recent change that deduplicates prefixes, which accidentally strips variant suffixes when upstream proxy injects `:fast` or `:large`. Cache key builder used the normalized prefix and appended only the base model name, not the full model id.

sophia: So two separate issues converging: (1) proxy/model rewrite leading to two models sending identical cache namespace, (2) cache key generation dropping the exact model variant and not including vector dimensionality. Result = cross-model cache hits returning vectors of the wrong size.

jess: Short-term mitigation for affected tenant: flush cache namespace for acme-123, and set a tenant-level cache-policy to bypass cache while we roll a fix. I can run the flush.

ai-support-bot: Created incident INC-3456 and attached logs. (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-3456)

customer-ops-bob: Please do, customers are hitting ingestion errors in prod. They can't index until dims are consistent.

jess: Flushed cache for acme-123: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "*acme-123*" | xargs redis-cli del` — confirmed ~480 keys removed. Asking them to retry.

customer-ops-bob: They retried and report no more mismatch errors for ~10 mins. But they want a permanent fix.

matt: Fix plan: 1) patch cache key to include full model id (including variant suffix), model_version, and vector_dim; 2) add guard that rejects cached vector if dim != expected (fail-safe); 3) add unit/integration test that simulates model rewrite + prefix normalization collision. I'll PR today.

sophia: Also add monitoring: emit a metric cache.dim_mismatch_count with labels tenant/model so we can alert before ingestion errors.

jess: I'm adding a temporary rule on the proxy to stop rewriting model param until the deploy is safe. Canary paused.

matt: Rolling patch to runtime and SDK. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/782 (WIP). I'll tag eng-ml and eng-runtime for review.

customer-ops-bob: Customer asked if this could cause billing surprises (cached vector reused across variants). Can we confirm billing is tied to request model actually executed, not cache hits?

sophia: Billing only counts the final served tokens/embeddings. If we returned a cached vector created from another model but served it, that would be a correctness issue but billing records show the model that responded. We should audit a few requests; I'll open billing-audit ticket.

jess: Follow-ups:
- matt to finish PR and include dim in cache keys (owner: matt)
- sophia to add metrics + billing audit (owner: sophia)
- jess to monitor acme-123 for 24h and keep canary paused
- customer-ops-bob to update customer and confirm post-fix

ai-support-bot: INC-3456 updated: assigned to matt, severity S2.

matt: ETA: hotfix today for runtime + SDK, full rollout tomorrow with tests. If anyone sees any other tenants with similar flakiness, drop them here.

customer-ops-bob: Thanks all, customer flagged as high priority. They'll reach back after next run. :thumbsup:
